newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Pepsico details NZ restaurant offer.
newsitem.headline: Pepsico details NZ restaurant offer.

text.p: Investors will be offered 85 million shares in a new company formed to control Pepsico Inc's 122 New Zealand KFC and Pizza Hut outlets, the company, Restaurant Brands Ltd, said on Thursday.
Restaurant Brands said it had acquired the outlets from Pepsico as part of that company's concentration on franchising and brand development.
The offer price of the shares, representing 100 percent of Restaurant Brands' capital, would be determined by tenders from domestic and international institutions.
The expected range was NZ$1.80 to $2.20 a share. All investors will pay the same price under the offer.
The minimum application for retail investors is 500 shares with applications closing May 30. Institutional tenders close on June 3 with the company expected to list on June 4.
In the year to November 30, the combined KFC-Pizza Hut operations reported record earnings before interest, tax and amortisation (EBITA) of NZ$20 million on sales of $221 million.
Earnings were expected to rise to NZ$24 million and $27.7 million in the 1997 and 1998 years respectively.
The float will be the largest since Tranz Rail in June last year, and the first listed investment in the restaurant and service sector.
Both businesses will operate under long-term international KFC and Pizza Hut franchise agreements.
They will be run by Jim Collier, who has held management responsibility for them for the past two years.

Chairman Bill Falconer said the combined operations had a strong and consistent record of growth, with KFC producing compound annual sales and pre-tax earnings growth of 12 percent and 18 percent respectively over the past five years.
Pizza Hut, acquired from its former franchisee in January 1995, was re-positioning its menu and pricing in with international Pizza Hut norms, he said.
Collier said the company had a strategy of developing new stores and increasing capacity at existing stores.

The company expects to pay out 70 percent of profits in fully-imputed dividends, with the 1998 dividend forecast at 11.4 cents a share. At the mid-point of the share price range, that would represent a gross dividend yield of 8.5 percent.
